replace.geometry_query:
Compute metric geometry from one policy-visible camera's published RGB-D and calibration: project world points to pixels, back-project pixels to world points, or summarise the valid depth of a rectangle.
Use when: a geometric quantity must be derived from calibration rather than estimated from the picture. The clearest case is world_points_m, which is the only way to ask where a world coordinate you already hold falls in an image -- for locating the commanded TCP target, a planned waypoint or a proposal's pregrasp point in the view you are looking at, and for reading whether it is in front of the camera and inside the frame. region answers "how deep is this patch" over a rectangle without naming a pixel. Near miss against mark_point: if you want a pixel measured, kept under a name and re-checked against a complementary view, call mark_point -- it verifies a repeated name across views (a disagreement beyond 25 mm fails that entry), reports depth-support counts and draws the overlay. This tool's points is the same back-projection without the mark, the name, the cross-view check or the image; prefer it when you want the number now and nothing retained, or when the pixel belongs to a saved step rather than the current observation.
Effect: read-only. It does not move the robot, change the scene, consume a robot decision, return any image, or persist a mark or reference; it reads the already-published observation artifacts and their calibration and returns numbers. Every result names the step and the source state it was computed from, and world_points_m additionally names the calibration hash it used.
Returns: exactly one of world_points, points or region_result, alongside step, source_state_sha256 and camera. world_points gives, per requested point, its camera-frame coordinates, in_front, in_frame, and -- when it is in front of the camera -- exact and rounded pixel_uv plus the scene depth already at that pixel and the residual between the two. points gives, per requested pixel, valid plus the median depth, the supporting sample count and world_xyz_m when depth was usable. region_result gives the rectangle, its valid sample count and fraction, and min/median/max depth when any sample was valid.
Does not: identify or segment an object, decide visibility or occlusion, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or task success. A positive depth_residual_m means the scene surface at that pixel is nearer than your point, which is evidence of occlusion and not a verdict on it; in_frame is image bounds, not line of sight. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, never an object centre or its hidden extent, and no returned number is simulator ground truth.
On error: send exactly one of points, region or world_points_m -- none or two is refused and the message names all three. Use the named view's own top-left OpenCV pixel frame, keep every pixel and the whole rectangle inside that image, and order the rectangle [x0,y0,x1,y1] with x0<x1 and y0<y1. Missing or invalid depth is reported, never inferred, and does not fail the call: a points entry returns valid false with no depth or world_xyz_m, region_result reports valid_count 0 with no depth_m, and a projected world point carries null scene_depth_m and depth_residual_m. To obtain a reading, move the pixel farther inside the intended surface, widen window_px, or read a complementary view. The camera list is fixed: agentview, wrist. The wrist moves with the arm, so its calibration is valid only at the pose it was captured at -- after any motion, query the fresh observation instead of reusing an earlier pixel from it. Adjacent calculation: use compute for arithmetic on already supplied world-frame numbers. Keep projection, back-projection and depth sampling here so they bind the selected observation and calibration.
replace.mark_point:
Measure up to eight visible pixels of one current RGB view as world-frame points in a single call.
Use when: one or more exact pixels — not an object identity, centre or full extent — must become world XYZ for a waypoint, clearance comparison or geometric fallback. Pass point_ids and points_uv index-aligned and of equal length, in the native top-left [x,y] coordinates of the named view, choosing pixels well inside the intended visible surface. For one pixel, pass one point_id and one points_uv entry in the same batch format.
Effect: read-only with respect to the world, but every measured pixel persists one observation-bound geometric mark under its point_id. Reusing a name already solved from another view verifies the new measurement against the stored one instead of replacing it; a disagreement beyond 25 mm fails only that entry, with error_code inconsistent_mark, and keeps the stored measurement.
Returns: a call status of solved, partial or failed, plus one marks[] entry per requested pixel in request order, each repeating its own source_index. An entry carries its own status, xyz_m in metres when it solved, the distinct views that measured that name, and its depth-support evidence — measured depth, window radius, valid, supporting and rejected sample counts, and maximum support deviation — on success and on failure alike. The call returns one composite overlay: each entry names the colour_rgb it was drawn in, and image_mapping binds a panel to a source_index rather than to its position, because inline images are evicted one block at a time. Measurement feedback states coordinate units and limitations; null residuals are unmeasured.
Does not: track a pixel through robot or camera motion, segment or identify the object, infer hidden geometry, correct a click on the wrong surface, expose simulator ground truth, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or success. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, not an object centre, and eight measured pixels are not a shape.
On error: a malformed call — unequal lengths, a repeated name, more than eight entries, or a view that cannot be marked — is refused whole and names the field, while a pixel that cannot be measured fails only its own entry and leaves the rest solved. Read that entry's error_code: aim farther inside the surface for depth_discontinuity or insufficient_depth_support, choose a different pixel for invalid_depth at the camera far plane, and resolve a disputed name from a complementary current view. A wrist camera moves with its arm, so after any motion discard old wrist pixels and query the fresh observation rather than hand-projecting the old image location.
replace.grasp_plan:
Generate inspectable public RGB-D grasp candidates for one current target.
Use when: current grounding or segmentation identifies the intended object and you need parallel-jaw poses.
Effect: read-only; queries Contact-GraspNet using the selected source-camera RGB-D and compiles poses to the public TCP convention. Optional synchronized views provide review evidence.
Returns: up to three candidates, complete world-frame pregrasp_pose and contact_pose, copyable bounded contact_approach targets, predicted opening, compiler checks and labeled review images. Reachability is delegated to move_pose. Inspect every candidate panel and choose target identity and geometry independently of rank. For this atomic surface, command the selected pregrasp_pose with move_pose, then read the receipt and fresh observation before approaching or closing with set_gripper. Re-plan candidates after any world action. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Send these fields at the top level. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}
Does not: plan trajectories, certify reachability, move the robot, command a gripper, use object ground truth, certify retention or report task success. Backend rank is not a success probability. Missing optional review cameras do not invalidate usable primary input.
On error: obtain a better current view or select another target or candidate. Recompute after the target or observation changes. After a submitted motion fails, use its phase and measured residual to choose the next action. Retention evidence remains advisory.
replace.move_pose:
Submit a complete pose target through the Supervisor.
Use when: moving the public TCP to a stated position and orientation. This surface drives one right arm: send the target fields directly, with no targets wrapper and no arm choice. Each arm names its two choices as enums -- position_mode (hold_current, absolute, delta) and orientation_mode (hold_current, absolute_quaternion, axis_angle_delta) -- and sends that mode's fields beside them in the arguments themselves. absolute takes position_m; delta takes translation_m and position_frame; absolute_quaternion takes orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta takes rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg and orientation_frame -- rotation_angle_deg is in DEGREES, and no field here takes radians. To hold one half while changing the other, set its mode to hold_current. Label the target free_space, precision or contact_approach by physical intent, not by controller name.
Effect: compiles the request once. free_space uses global CuRobo. precision within 50 mm and 15 degrees uses bounded OSC; larger precision uses global CuRobo. contact_approach within 50 mm and 15 degrees uses bounded OSC. A larger contact_approach is staged: global CuRobo to a pre-contact pose on the way that leaves at most 35 mm and 10 degrees, then bounded OSC for the rest. The local segment runs only after the pre-contact segment converges; otherwise the receipt's precontact field names why, and the arm stays where that segment ended. A failed local route never silently falls back to global.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival, and available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to choose CuRobo versus local OSC; change an exact requested orientation; command a gripper; move an omitted arm; infer contact, retention or task success; retry a failed local stage through another backend.
On error: an argument refusal names the field and the bound it violated, never a branch index. position_mode delta without translation_m is refused at translation_m; a field belonging to another mode is refused by name. planner_failed describes a bounded planner search failure; planning_diagnostics distinguishes target IK convergence/admission from trajectory search when the backend exposes it; plan_rejected means zero controller writes; not_reached means execution started but measured convergence or endpoint verification failed. Use the named phase and fresh evidence rather than repeating the same target blindly. Failure diagnosis: planner_error identifies a failed planner service or implementation, not an unreachable target; invalid_start_state requires correcting the measured start; planner_failed reports ordinary search failure. not_reached preserves endpoint and controller evidence independently of official task termination. Read the fresh observation before proposing another action. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.move_to:
Move the right grip site to a world-frame position while holding the measured action-start orientation.
Use when: the intended change is translation-only free-space repositioning and orientation is already suitable.
Effect: world mutation; compiles through canonical move_pose with interaction free_space, so the qualified global CuRobo route executes it. One robot decision.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: rotate, command the gripper, take an arm choice, or guarantee reachability; endpoint arrival does not prove alignment or contact.
On error: inspect the named failure stage and residual, pick a reachable intermediate position, or use recover_pose after a genuine motion failure. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.rotate_pitch:
Tilt the current approach axis while holding position.
Use when: rotating the right grip site about its lateral axis (Panda local +Y) while holding position — for example tilting the approach direction between top-down and side grasps.
Effect: compiles the signed angle to an exact pose through canonical move_pose; small rotations execute through the bounded OSC servo, larger ones through global CuRobo. One robot decision.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: translate, command the gripper, or prove the new approach direction clears obstacles — verify from a fresh observation.
On error: check the current grip-site axes and correct the sign or magnitude; use move_pose when position must change together with orientation. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.rotate_wrist:
Rotate the jaw line around the current approach axis while holding position.
Use when: rotating the right grip site about its approach axis (Panda local +Z, pointing out of the gripper) while holding position — usually to align the jaw-closing line with an object's grasp axis before descending.
Effect: compiles the signed angle to an exact pose through canonical move_pose. Small rotations execute through the bounded OSC servo; larger rotations execute through global CuRobo. One robot decision.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: expose a literal wrist joint, translate, command the gripper, or verify that the jaws actually align with the object — confirm alignment from a fresh observation.
On error: check the current grip-site axes and correct the sign or magnitude; after a substantial rotation re-observe before descending. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.recover_pose:
Plan the right arm to a named robot-only recovery configuration while preserving the gripper command.
Use when: a planner or execution failure, or a poor configuration, makes ordinary waypoint correction inappropriate; choose previous to return to the joints measured at the start of the last motion action, or home for a deliberate return to the source-bound start configuration.
Effect: world mutation through the qualified global CuRobo recovery route. One robot decision.
Returns: the submitted strategy; the next receipt and fresh observation report actual planning, residuals and preservation evidence. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values.
Does not: reset the episode, restore moved objects or evaluator state, release the gripper, reverse an old trajectory, act as an emergency stop, or guarantee escape from contact.
On error: if the recovery state is unavailable the call is refused; try the other strategy only when physically sensible, otherwise finish with failure honestly.
